target_customer: Teens and young adults using live video to meet friends
problem: Social video calling to talk with friends and meet new people.

founders.name: Mike McIntyre
founders.background_notes: YC page: product manager on growth, search ranking and Safety Check.

competitors.name: Houseparty
competitors.traction_then: Described by TechCrunch in 2017-03 as a leading private video hangout app

technical_complexity.rationale: Live video with matching and moderation for a teen audience needs real-time video infrastructure and safety tooling.

defensibility.rationale: Social graph effects possible but Houseparty and big social apps could offer live video.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Group video features were added by large platforms; no source on action against this Fam.

market_need_then: Group video apps like Houseparty were growing in 2016 and 2017; no data on this Fam's own demand found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Youthful and creator oriented; the site features Fambassador creator profiles.

branding.brand_signature: Fambassadors creator program on the site

rebrands.why: YC page says the company was in the batch under FriendSpot; no reason given.

branding.community_and_virality: Site shows a Fambassadors creator row and TikTok and Instagram accounts; scale not sourced.

brand_strength.rationale: A short friendly name but shared with other apps called Fam, including an unrelated 2016 iMessage app from Smack, and little brand press found.

pivots.from: FriendSpot, a group messaging app for meeting friends in person
pivots.why: Not stated; the FriendSpot description comes from a search snippet of a database profile

outcome_analysis: Fam went through YC in Summer 2017 under the FriendSpot name and later raised a Series A led by Founders Fund; totals are reported at 15 to 18 million dollars by differing sources. YC lists it Inactive while the website and App Store listing from SpotMap still exist, so the status is unclear and no failure cause is public.
notes: Name collision: the 2016 Boston iMessage group video app Fam by Smack (founders Giuseppe Stuto and others, 1.8M raised 2017-03) is a different company and is not recorded as a round here. The Series A for this Fam has no found date or amount; total raised 15M (CB Insights, one database) or over 18M (a company statement in a profile, not opened) so earlier rounds may be missing. Education not found. Houseparty is cited via an article about the other Fam, dated within the batch year.
